recent_fixes_2026_06_04: Auto-includes are madc-mode only: Program::set_language_standard_option centralizes --std parsing for CLI and shebangs, recognizes C and C++ standards, and Program::auto_includes_enabled gates pending embedded header collection/injection to STD_MADC. --std=c and --std=c++ now require explicit includes; tests/teststdcppinclude.mad covers explicit --std=c++ use.

Generic external bool returns: CIR external prototypes now emit N_BOOL for dtBOOL scalar/return specs instead of long/int. This fixes bool-returning external functions and methods without class-specific handling; test_cir has an extern C bool host-symbol probe and teststringmethods produces the expected empty() values.

Generic range-for element locals: CIR block lowering skips parameters by explicit vfPARAM flag instead of parameter-count position, so compiler-generated range-for element variables are declared and constructed in functions with parameters, including included/header function bodies. tests/testforeachheaderbody.mad covers this path.

Extern C/C++ linkage specs parse as declaration modifiers for single declarations and blocks. Generic object-return call classification now excludes reference-returning functions from the retbuf path, avoiding bogus hidden return-slot arguments. tests/testexternclinkage.mad covers the parser path and a class-reference returning call.

Function signatures preserve source typedef aliases through FuncDef for return types and parameters. CIR user prototypes, definitions, function-pointer signatures, and referenced external prototypes now render declaration-only extern C functions with header spelling such as string * instead of falling back through raw DataDef rendering. tests/testexterncstringptr.mad covers a C ABI string-pointer wrapper used from an ordinary namespace function.

Embedded <ns_php> now declares __php_* runtime symbols as explicit extern C ABI functions and implements php:: calls as ordinary namespace wrapper bodies. testphp.mad and --emit=c11 testphp show generated __ns_php_* wrappers over the C ABI boundary, not direct asm aliases on the C++ namespace surface.

Embedded <ns_perl> now declares __perl_* runtime symbols as explicit extern C ABI functions and implements perl:: calls as ordinary namespace wrapper bodies. testperl.mad, testregex.mad, testprefer.mad, and --emit=c11 testperl show generated __ns_perl_* wrappers over the C ABI boundary.

Embedded <ns_python>, <ns_ruby>, and <ns_js> now declare runtime symbols as explicit extern C ABI functions and implement namespace calls as ordinary wrapper bodies. testlang.mad, testrubycharsshadow.mad, and --emit=c11 testlang show generated __ns_python_*, __ns_ruby_*, and __ns_js_* wrappers.

Embedded <ns_rust> now declares __rust_* runtime symbols as explicit extern C ABI functions and implements rust:: calls as ordinary namespace wrapper bodies; rust::match remains parser syntax. testrust.mad, testrustmatch.mad, testprefer.mad, and --emit=c11 testrust show generated __ns_rust_* wrappers.
recent_fixes_2026_06_02: STRUCT EARNS CLASS-HOOD (78d1b27, madc parser only): teststruct2 SIGSEGV'd because a std::string MEMBER of a struct was never constructed. In C++ a struct IS a class (differ only in default access); the CONTENTS decide object semantics, not the keyword. A struct now stays a DataDefSTRUCT and is PROMOTED to a DataDefCLASS (which is-a DataDefSTRUCT) at the closing `}` when it has an object member by value (is_object(); std::string is an object) -> flows through the existing class member-ctor/RAII-dtor machinery. Trivial structs (no object members) are unchanged. Because only object-having structs promote, trivial C structs (all gcc.c-torture + SMAUG) are untouched -> ZERO regression (the blanket 'every struct is a class' attempts failed at 65-113 regressions by flooding the class path with trivial structs+builtins like __madc_va_list_tag; promotion avoids that). Integration 456->457; torture 1565 zero-regr; SMAUG boots. ~28 lines, no cir_builder/datadef/fork change. NOTE std::string is NOT a trivial struct -- it is_object() (has ctors/dtors/overloads), keeps full object treatment.
